title: The Quack Toad

full_text:
An ugly, warty toad crawled out from his muddy swamp, climbed upon a stone in the meadow, and announced to all the woodland beasts that he was a master physician who possessed secret panaceas to cure every disease under the sun.

The woodland animals gathered around in awe, marveling at his boastful medical claims.

A clever fox stepped forward, examined the toad's blotched, wrinkled skin, his swollen throat, and his watery eyes, and laughed:

"Look at yourself, quack! How can you presume to cure others of palsy and pestilence when you cannot even cure your own blotched skin and limping crawl? Heal yourself first before offering medicine to the forest!"
moral: Physician, heal thyself before you presume to cure the infirmities of others.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
